name: Trello
description: Read-only Trello access: member identity, boards, lists and cards

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the Trello member the credential belongs to (username, full name, member URL)

tools.name: list_boards
tools.description: List the Trello boards the credential's member can see, optionally filtered by board state

tools.name: list_lists
tools.description: List the lists (columns) on one Trello board

filter.description: Optional list filter (default open lists as returned by Trello)

tools.name: list_cards
tools.description: List the cards in one Trello list

tools.name: get_card
tools.description: Get one Trello card by ID (name, description, due date, labels, parent list and board)

needs_review: DUAL-QUERY AUTH WORKAROUND (documented pattern, reusable): Trello authenticates with TWO query parameters, key and token, per its own OpenAPI securitySchemes (APIKey in=query name=key, APIToken in=query name=token at https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/trello/swagger.v3.json). Spec v1 auth.type 'query' carries exactly ONE parameter, so the key rides in auth ({type: query, param: key, field: api_key}) and the token rides as a "token": "{{token}}" placeholder in the request.query of EVERY tool and in test.query. Both placeholder names are the real vault field names from integrationTypeRegistry.js key trello (api_key, token), so no field mapping is involved. Placeholders referencing requiredFields are legal in query values, so this is inside the contract rather than an escape hatch; any future two-parameter query API should copy it. The cost: the second parameter is per-tool, so a new tool that omits "token" will fail at runtime with a 401 rather than at validation time.

NO PAGING OR LIMIT INPUTS: none of the five read routes documents a limit, page or page_size parameter in the Trello OpenAPI (/members/{id}, /members/{id}/boards, /boards/{id}/lists, /lists/{id}/cards, /cards/{id}), so no clamp helper is used. Volume is bounded by response.truncate 2000 only. Trello's optional 'fields' parameter is documented on several of these routes but is deliberately not exposed: response.pick already selects the fields, and a caller-supplied fields list would silently empty those picks.

BLIND SHAPE PROOF ONLY: no Trello account is held, so board, list and card identifiers are opaque and cannot be probed. No _probe hints are supplied, because a made-up identifier cannot route; the proof file records what the dummy credential actually returned rather than guessing.
